description: React + Vite multimodal client — three concurrent inputs (text prompt, dropped image, recorded audio) are packed into a single multipart POST to /api/multimodal, and the multimodal LLM's streamed response renders back in the composer. For building GPT-4o/Claude/Gemini multimodal clients without picking a vendor SDK.

defaults.headline: One message, three modalities
defaults.subheadline: Drop an image, record 3 seconds of audio, type your question. Send — the multimodal LLM sees all three.

gotchas: multipart/form-data is the only format all three big multimodal APIs accept without re-encoding. Don't wrap image + audio in a JSON body — base64 + UTF-8 overhead bloats payloads and breaks streaming.

React 19 Strict Mode runs effects twice in dev — if you kick off getUserMedia inside useEffect without a cleanup, the second call races the first and you get NotReadableError. Always return a cleanup that stops the tracks.
Dropped files trigger both `dragover` and `drop` — you MUST preventDefault on dragover or the browser will navigate to the file instead of firing your drop handler.

Recording audio AND previewing an image AND typing text in the same component means three independent state machines. Keep them in separate useState hooks — one merged state object leads to stale-closure bugs.
The <audio>/<video> preview elements need `URL.revokeObjectURL` when the user re-records or removes the file, else Chrome leaks ~50MB per blob until GC eventually fires.
Safari's DataTransferItemList only exposes files synchronously inside the drop handler. If you await anything before reading `e.dataTransfer.files`, the list is already cleared.
